613:
The Georgetown-Quitman County Government prohibits its elected officials, appointed officials and employees from accepting gifts or gratuities from individuals or firms related to county government business. The acceptance of such gifts are unprofessional, unbusinesslike, and places elected officials, appointed officials and county employees in compromising positions, which are not in the best interest of the county government. It is also against county policy to give gifts to businesses and others that do business with the county government. No county funds may be used for funeral or retirement expenses.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
614:
(a) Paychecks will be distributed by your manager, payroll or personnel department after 11:00 p.m. on Friday. For the exception of employees working a four day workweek, pick up time will be after 3:00 p.m. on Thursday.
(b) Georgetown-Quitman County Commission will not release your paycheck to another individual (other than those mentioned above) without your permission. Georgetown-Quitman County Commission will not release or issue your paycheck in advance of the normal distribution schedule without prior authorization of the manager, payroll or personnel department.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
615:
(a) Exempt employees. Exempt employees are paid on a salary basis, i.e., their compensation is not based on the number of hours worked. Exempt full-time employees are expected to average working at least 40 hours per week, but to spend the hours necessary to complete their job responsibilities. Those hours worked in excess of an average of 40 hours per week will be counted as compensatory time. See compensatory time.
(b) Compensatory time.
(1) For exempt employees who must often work long hours in performing the job requirements of their position, a compensatory time leave is provided as a convenience, but not a mandatory right for such employees. Such leave must have the written approval of the supervisor or county manager. Failure to get proper advance approval can cause the time charged to annual leave, a salary reduction, or a reprimand.
(2) Compensatory time leave will be granted at the convenience of Georgetown-Quitman County and must not conflict with accomplishment of job duties and responsibilities.
(3) A maximum of ten days of compensatory time leave may be accumulated and carried over into a new calendar year.
(4) Hours within 15 minutes prior to opening and 15 minutes after normal closing hours are not used in calculating compensatory time, unless the overtime is in excess of these times.
(c) Deductions from salaries. Under the provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act no deductions may be made from the salary of any executive, administrative, or professional employee for time lost in any week in which the employee does any work, unless the time lost is:
(1) An absence of a day or more for personal reasons other than sickness or accident; or
(2) An absence of a day or more for illness or if the employee's attendance is unsatisfactory.
(3) A deduction may be made to offset payment received for court or military duty.
(4) The employee does not maintain an average of 40 hours per week during the work year.
(d) Supplements to salary. Since time on the job is not the basis for compensating exempt employees, there will normally be no additional compensation for time worked beyond regularly scheduled hours. In the unusual circumstance that satisfactory performance of assigned responsibility mandates time on the job substantially in excess of regular hours, the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County, may approve supplemental payment to compensate the employee for personal time lost.
(e) Reimbursement for dinner and lunch.
(1) Exempt employees shall be reimbursed for dinner within a limit established by the county manager, provided that an employee works at least 2½ hours or more beyond the close of the normal workday and/or is outside the Quitman County, Georgetown, Eufaula area.
(2) Lunch expense may be reimbursed up to a limit established by the County Commission, provided that an employee works at least four hours on a Saturday, Sunday, or holiday. Receipts are required.
(3) Exempt county employees include elected officials: Tax commissioner, sheriff, clerk to sheriff's department, probate judge, clerk or courts, and county commissioners. The county nonelected employee positions are: County clerk, county treasurer, sheriff's deputy, county agent, and clerk to probate judge/voter registrar, fire chief and assistant fire chief.
(f) Nonexempt employees. All nonexempt employees are paid on the basis of hours worked. Nonexempt employees will be compensated on the basis of the total number of hours worked during a given week:
(1) Up to 40 hours: All work performed up to 40 hours in a single week will be at the straight-time hourly rate, regardless of the length of the regular workweek.
(2) Over 40 hours: In excess of 40 hours in a single week will be paid at 1½ times the straight-time hourly rate. The nonexempt employees of Georgetown-Quitman County, GA. include: Janitor (part-time), clerk to tax commissioner (full-time/part-time), landfill general worker (part-time) working public works superintendent, working assistant public works superintendent, working mechanic, general worker (3), transit driver substitute transit driver, clerk to county agent, dispatchers for sheriff (part-time) (2), building inspector, assistant county clerk, clerk to tax appraiser, landfill operator, clerk/dispatcher for sheriff, and deputy clerk of courts (part-time).
(g) Time worked. The following provisions apply to the calculating of nonexempt employee hours' worked:
(1) Lunch or supper periods: Time off for lunch or supper is not counted as time worked.
(2) Paid holidays and paid absences: Regularly observed paid holidays and approved paid absences are counted as time worked. Hours of work performed on regularly paid holiday will also be counted.
(3) Approved rest or restrooms periods of from five to 20 minutes duration are counted as time worked.
(h) Early arrivals and late departures. The Federal Fair Labor Standards Act recognizes a reasonable time for getting to and from work stations, which time is considered as hours worked. Georgetown-Quitman County has interpreted "reasonable time" as 15 minutes prior to and following scheduled opening and closing hours. All employees should not arrive at work stations or record their time earlier than 15 minutes before starting time, or not to remain on the premises after closing time, unless permission has been granted for overtime.
(i) Work away from premises or at home. A nonexempt employee shall not be permitted to perform work at home, unless approved in advance by the supervisor. If approved, work performed off the premises, job site or at home by a nonexempt employee may be counted as time worked.
(j) Travel. Time spent in travel between the employees' home, and normal work location is not counted as time worked. However, when the employee travels to a special assignment in another county, the time spent traveling in excess of normal commuting time is counted as hours worked.
(k) Time records for nonexempt employees.
(1) The Federal Labor Standards Act plus state laws require that Georgetown-Quitman County, GA. keep records worked by nonexempt employees. These time records serve as evidence that Georgetown-Quitman County is conforming with the laws in its working hours and are a basis on which overtime is paid under the Federal Fair Labor Standards Act.
(2) Time records must be complete and accurate. The maintenance of inaccurate records or the misrepresentation of the amount of time worked is a violation of the law.
(l) Wage and salary changes. All recommendations for wage or salary increases of exempt or nonexempt employees shall be based on the employee's value to the Georgetown-Quitman County Government, as defined by the periodic evaluation of the job and the employee's demonstrated level of performance.
(1) An absence of a day or more for illness or if the employee's attendance is unsatisfactory.
(2) A deduction may be made to offset payment received for court or military duty.
(3) The employee does not maintain an average of 40 hours per week during the work year.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
616:
Solicitations for contributions, sale of merchandise, circulation of petitions, solicitation of membership in clubs and organizations and all other forms of solicitations by employees are prohibited during office hours.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
617:
(a) Employees should operate in a manner both safe to themselves and their fellow workers; should report changes in his/her address or family status to their supervisor/county clerk, and should periodically check county bulletin boards for employee information.
(b) Employees should not work in a manner that willfully obstructs or hinders other employees from completing their assigned duties; personal problems should not be pursued at work; telephones should not be used for personal telephone calls; and employees should not have personal visitors, unless permission is obtained.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
618:
Although no formal dress code exists, you are asked to wear articles of clothing suitable to the type of work you do and the work environment in which you work. Articles of clothing should be neat, clean, in good taste, and not constitute a safety hazard.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
619:
(a) An employee's relatives will not be employed by the Georgetown-Quitman County Commission under any of the following circumstances:
(1) Where one of the parties would have authority (or practical power) to supervise, appoint, remove or discipline the other;
(2) Where one party would be responsible for auditing the work of the other;
(3) Where both parties would report to the same immediate supervisor (except in the case of temporary employees, in which case the employment may be allowed by the county manager); or
(4) Where other circumstances might lead to potential conflict among the parties or conflict between the interest of one or both parties and the best interests of the county.
(b) "Relatives" include an employee's parent, child, spouse, brother, sister-in-laws and step relationships.
(c) If two employees marry, become related or begin sharing living quarters with one another, and in the county's judgment one or more of the potential problems noted above exist or reasonably could exist, only one of the employees will be permitted to stay with the county, unless reasonable accommodations, as determined by the county manager, can be made to eliminate the potential problem. The decision as to which relative will remain with the county must be made by the two employees within 30 calendar days of the date they marry, become related, or begin sharing living quarters with each other. If no decision has been made during this time, the county reserves the right to terminate either employee.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
620:
(a) It is the policy the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County, that its workplace shall be drug-free in compliance with the Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988 (PL100-690, Title V, Subtitle D).
(b) The policy of Georgetown-Quitman County, GA., no employee shall engage in the unlawful manufacture, distribution, dispensing, possession or the use of a controlled substance in the workplace.
(c) Each employee is instructed to hereby notify their supervisor and the county clerk of any criminal drug statute conviction for a violation in the workplace. Within 30 days, the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County, GA. must take action as appropriate.
(d) Any employee violating the terms of this policy is subject to immediate dismissal. Employees found to be abusing drugs, but not convicted of any drug statute violation, will be subject to progressive discipline and required to satisfactorily participate in a rehabilitation program approved for such purpose at the employee's expense.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
621:
For health and safety considerations, Georgetown-Quitman County prohibits smoking by employees in all Georgetown-Quitman County the facilities, including Georgetown-Quitman County-owned buildings, vehicles, and offices or other facilities rented or leased by Georgetown-Quitman County, including individual employee offices.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
622:
(a) Georgetown-Quitman County, GA. is an equal employment employer. Our long-stated policy has been clearly and simply stated as follows:
(b) Georgetown-Quitman County, GA. reaffirms its policy treating all employees and applicants, whether or not they are members of minority groups, equally according to their individual qualifications, ability, experience, and other employment standards. There is to be no discrimination because of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, age, handicapped or veteran status.
(c) It is equally the practice and policy of the Georgetown-Quitman County, GA. local government to comply with applicable federal, state and local labor laws.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
623:
Georgetown-Quitman County funds shall not be expended for funeral or hospital flowers/gifts of employees/elected officials/or their families. Local voluntary employee contribution hospitality clubs are encouraged to pay for such items, including retirement parties.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
624:
Georgetown-Quitman County takes a position that gambling among its employees can lead to bad morale, hard feelings and financial hardships. Therefore, gambling is prohibited on county premises and will be a cause for discipline. This includes card playing, dice, and other wagering. Any employee who is guilty of selling or attempting to sell football pools will be subject to discipline.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
625:
(a) A garnishment is a legal action by a creditor requiring Georgetown-Quitman County, GA. to withhold an amount from an employee's earnings. Georgetown-Quitman County must forward the amount to the creditor each payday until the debt has been paid.
(b) When a garnishment is served on Georgetown-Quitman County, GA., the employee shall be contacted by the county clerk. The employee shall be asked to try to make an arrangement with the creditor to make direct payments to satisfy the indebtedness. If an agreement is reached, the employee will ask the creditor to issue a written release to Georgetown-Quitman County, GA.
(c) If no release is received, or if, after receipt of a release the employee reneges on the agreement, Georgetown-Quitman County, GA. must process the garnishment.
(d) Employees whose earnings are garnished or levied will be counseled on the wisdom of managing their personal affairs so as not to involve Georgetown-Quitman County. Garnishments against county employees leave a negative public view on all county employees in the community.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
626:
(a) A grievance is a complaint you may have about your hours of work, your rights under personnel policies, your wages, seemingly unfair or unequal treatment or discipline, or other problems related to your employment.
(b) Policy. It is policy of Georgetown-Quitman County to foster employee satisfaction and to give careful consideration and attention to any complaint. For the purposes of this rule, a grievance shall be considered to be any matter concerning an employee's status or conditions of employment for which appeal is not provided, or prohibited, in these rules and regulations.
(c) Informal grievance procedure. An employee who has a problem or complaint should first try to get it settled through discussion with his immediate supervisor without delay. If, after this discussion, he does not believe the problem has been satisfactorily resolved, he shall have the right to discuss it with his supervisor's immediate superior, if any, in the administrative service. Every effort should be made to find an acceptable solution by informal means at the lowest possible level of supervision. If the employee is not in agreement with the decision reached by discussion, he shall then have the right to file a formal grievance in writing within five work days after receiving the informal decision or decisions. An informal grievance shall not be taken above the department head.
(d) Formal grievance procedure.
(1) First level of review. A grievance shall be presented in writing to the employee's immediate supervisor, who shall render his decision and comments in writing and return them to the employee within five work days after receiving the grievance. If the employee does not agree with his supervisor's decision, or the immediate supervisor fails to provide resolution of the grievance as outlined above, the employee may present the appeal in writing to his supervisor's immediate supervisor. Failure of the employee to do so with five work days after receipt of the written decision of his superior, or within ten work days if no decision is rendered will constitute a withdrawal of the grievance.
(2) Further level or levels of review as appropriate. The supervisor receiving the grievance shall review it, render his decision and comment in writing, and return to the employee within five work days after receiving it. If the employee does not agree with the decision, or if no answer has been received within five work days after the supervisor receives the grievance, the employee may present the appeal in writing to the department head. Failure of the employee to take further action within five work days after receipt of the written decision of the supervisor, or within ten work days if no decision is rendered will constitute a withdrawal of the grievance.
(3) Department review. The department head receiving the grievance, or his designated representative, shall discuss the grievance with the employee, his representative, if any, and with other appropriate persons. The department head shall render his decision and comments in writing, and return them to the employee within five days after receiving the appeal. If the employee does not agree with the decision reached, or if the department head fails to provide resolution of the grievance as outlined above, he may present his appeal in writing to the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County. Failure of the employee to take further action within five days after receipt of the written decision of the department head, or within ten work days if no decision is rendered shall constitute a withdrawal of the grievance.
(4) County commission. The Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County, upon receiving the grievance, shall discuss the grievance with the employee, his representative, if any, and with other appropriate persons. The Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County shall render its decision and comments in writing, and return them to the employee within five work days after receiving the appeal. Decision of the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County is final.
(e) Conduct of grievance procedures.
(1) The time limits specified above may be extended to a definite date by mutual agreement of the employee and the reviewer concerned.
(2) The employee may request the assistance of another person of his own choosing in preparing and presenting his appeal at any level of review.
(3) The employee and his representative may be privileged to use a reasonable amount of work time as determined by the appropriate department head in conferring about and presenting the appeal.
(4) The employee shall be assured freedom from reprisal for using the grievance procedures.
(f) Employee counseling. At any time, an employee having a personnel problem may seek advice from his department head.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
627:
(a) Definition of appeal. For the purpose of these rules and regulations, appeal is the opportunity given an employee to request a hearing before the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County on a personnel action or matter which he believes adversely affects him when provision for such appeal is specifically provided in these rules and regulations (see rules on demotion, resignation, lay-off, suspension and dismissal).
(b) Employee eligible for appeal. Only a permanent-status career employee is eligible to appeal a personnel action and request a hearing before the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County, GA.
(c) Procedures for appeal. A permanent-status career employee, who has been adversely affected by a personnel action which may be appealed to the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County, GA., may appeal by filing a request in writing within five work days of notification of such adverse personnel action to the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County. It shall contain the employee's name, position, title, division, and department of office, and his home address. It shall also include the action complained of, a concise statement as to why the appeal is being filed, and such other information as may be required other provisions of these rules and regulations or which the employee believes to be directly related to the action being appealed. The Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County shall review the appeal and may consult with the employee's supervisor and department head if desired. They shall, within five work days after the receipt of the request for appeal, make a recombination.
(d) Commission decision on formal hearing. The Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County shall review the employee's appeal in all cases in which these rules provide for appeal to the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County as soon as possible. If it is decided to grant the employee a hearing, the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County shall notify him of the hearing date, time and location; if it decides not to grant the employee a hearing, the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County shall notify him of its decision on his appeal from the adverse personnel action, giving its reasons therefore. The decision of the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County on whether or not to grant a hearing in the case shall be final.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
628:
(a) Time limits. The Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County, GA. shall set the time, date and place for the hearing, which shall be no earlier that one week and not later than two weeks following commission's decision for allowing a hearing.
(b) Hearing procedure. Unless otherwise specified by the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County and stated in its notice, the hearing shall be conducted as follows:
(1) The department head, other administrative officials concerned, the county attorney, or other counsel representing the county service shall state the nature of the charge, that the action taken conforms with the provision of these rules, that such action is necessary and warranted and in the best interest of the county service; and he shall also present substantiating evidence.
(2) When it appears to the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County, that the charges have not been substantiated to its satisfaction, the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County may take whatever equitable action it deems necessary at the time.
(3) When the charges have been substantiated to the satisfaction of the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County, the appealing employee shall then be called upon to answer the charges and offer evidence in his behalf.
(4) The Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County, at its discretion, may permit rebuttal and surrebuttal.
(c) Conduct of hearing. The commission chairman or another member of the commission designated by the chairman to preside at the hearing has full authority at all times to maintain orderly procedure and restrict the hearing to relevant facts. All hearings shall be conducted in an orderly manner with a view of the presentation of all material and relevant facts so that a fair and impartial decision may be made. Commission members shall have the authority to seek diligently all information bearing on the case before, during and after any hearing. For the protection of the employee, hearings shall not be open to the public unless the employee specifically requests it.
(d) Informality of hearing proceedings. A hearing before the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County need not be conducted in the same manner as in a court of law, and informality in the matter of taking testimony or in any other hearing proceedings shall not affect the validity of any findings or decisions made by the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County, GA.
(e) Hearing continuance. Extension of time in scheduling a hearing or continuances in hearing may be granted or denied at the discretion of the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County, GA.
Note—If the personnel action recommended is termination, a hearing must be granted.
(f) Subpoena power. The Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County, GA. shall have the power to issue a subpoena and to require the attendance at a hearing of witnesses located within the county and the production by them of books, papers, and other materials pertinent to any matter of inquiry. A Georgetown-Quitman County Commission subpoena may be served by any person who could lawfully serve such subpoena in a civil case. A subpoena witness shall be paid the standard fee paid to a witness in county court. The Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County shall have the power to administer oaths and to examine all witnesses under oath in relation to any matter properly involved in a hearing.
(g) Employee witness. Employees of the Georgetown-Quitman County Government may be required by the commission to attend and testify at a hearing without subpoena and without remuneration. Failure to comply with such requirement shall constitute grounds for dismissal.
(h) Hearing of witnesses, depositions. Only witnesses having direct knowledge of the facts on which the charges are based will be heard by the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County, GA. Testimony of character witnesses will be received only in writing under oath, unless the commission agrees that the charges in the case involve moral or ethical issues in which cases, character witnesses and their cross-examination shall be allowed. At the discretion of the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County, statements of witnesses may be taken by written interrogatories or dispositions.
(i) Investigations. The Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County may direct that necessary investigations be made, and at its discretion it may conduct its own investigations.
(j) Record. At the discretion of the commission, a summary of verbatim record shall be made. The appealing employee may be supplied, at cost, a copy of the record.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
629:
(a) The county commission may decide an appeal it has heard in any manner that it deems necessary, appropriate, and in the best interest of the county service. The commission shall make its decision on an appeal as soon as possible after an appeal has been made and a hearing has been held. The same rules shall apply whenever the commission makes a decision on an employee's appeal without granting him a hearing. The county commission shall notify the appealing employee of its final decision on the appeal.
(b) Testimonial procedures.
(1) So that permanent-status career employees are afforded constitutional "due to process", department heads may not terminate an employee without pay.
(2) When an employee has been suspended the supervisor or department head shall immediately notify the personnel office, in writing, of the circumstances to include employee's name, department, offense(s), time(s), date(s), and a statement that there is sufficient written documentation available to warrant the suspension, and a recommendation for termination.
(3) From this information the personnel office will prepare a letter to the employee advising him that he has been suspended without pay pending a predetermination appeal hearing, the reason(s) for the suspension and recommended termination, that he has the right to a fair and impartial hearing, that he has the right to the counsel of his choice at his own expense if he so desires, and that he must request the appeal hearing in writing to the county commission, within five working days of his receipt of the letter or it will be assumed that he does not intend to request an appeal hearing and will be terminated effective with his date of suspension.
(4) The letter of notification will be sent certified mail, return receipt requested.
(5) If employee requests an appeal hearing, the appeal procedure Rule XII will be followed.
(6) Employees who are still in their probation period may be terminated for cause, by department heads.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
630:
(a) Discipline.
(1) All employees are expected to exercise good judgment, loyalty, common sense, dedication, and courtesy in the performance of their duties. The primary mission of every employee is to provide courteous, orderly, efficient, and economic delivery of services to the citizens of the county.
(2) Acts, errors or omissions which discredit the public service or impair the provision of orderly services to the citizens of the county may result in discipline, including termination.
(3) The county manager or supervisor, as appropriate, has full discretion and authority to impose disciplinary action in accordance with the county policy and the circumstances of the particular case.
(4) The following are examples of the types of behavior, which may result in discipline:
a. Drinking alcohol or the abuse of nonprescription or prescription drugs or other controlled substances on the job, or arriving on the job under the influence of or while in possession of alcohol, drugs, or other controlled substances.
b. Violation of a lawful duty.
c. Insubordination.
d. Absence from work without first notifying and securing permission from the supervisor.
e. Habitual absence or tardiness for any reason.
f. Unsatisfactory job performance, as determined by the county.
g. Conviction of a felony or a misdemeanor involving moral turpitude.
h. Acceptance of fees, gratuities or other valuable items in the performance of the employee's official duties for the county.
i. Inability, refusal or failure to perform the duties of the assigned job.
j. Violation of duties or rules imposed by this manual, or by any other county rule, regulation or administrative order.
(5) This list is not all-inclusive, but only serves as a general guide. The county may discipline or terminate employees for other reasons not stated above.
(6) In the event that discipline is necessary, the following types of disciplinary actions may be used, depending on the particular situation:
a. Oral warning. An oral warning is a counseling session between the employee's supervisor and the employee on the subject of the employee's conduct and performance, or his/her failure to observe a rule, regulation, or administrative instruction. It is intended to increase an employee's efficiency and value to the county by changing the employee's conduct, attitude, habits, or work methods. Following the counseling session the supervisor shall document the oral warning.
b. Reprimand. A reprimand is a formal written disciplinary action for misconduct, inadequate performance, or repeated lesser infractions. Written reprimands are placed in the employee's personnel file.
c. Suspension. A suspension is a temporary, unpaid absence from duty, which may be imposed as a penalty for significant misconduct or repeated lesser infractions. A suspension is a severe disciplinary action which is made part of the employee's permanent record.
(7) Suspensions with pay, where the employee is placed on administrative leave, may be utilized by the county manager pending the results of an investigation or disciplinary action where the county manager determines those factors such as public confidence, the safety of the employee or the efficient functioning of the county call for such a suspension.
(b) Termination.
(1) An employee may be terminated from county employment for any reasons listed below:
a. During or at the end of the employee's trial period.
b. As a result of disciplinary action.
c. Due to loss of skills, certifications or other conditions which would make the employee unfit for service.
d. When the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County has made a determination that a lack of work or funding exists with respect to the employee's position. The Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County has sole discretion to make determinations of lack of work or lack of funding.
e. If the employee has a physical or mental impairment that prevents him/her from performing the required duties of the employee's position and the employee cannot be reasonably accommodated. Termination must be supported by medical evidence, which establishes that the individual is unable to perform bona fide job requirements. The county may require an examination at its expense performed by a physician of its choice. Failure to submit to such request may result in termination.
(2) No employee will be disciplined or terminated for a discriminatory or otherwise illegal reason.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
631:
Upon resignation or termination, any accrued unused annual leave will be included in the employee's final pay calculation. The final pay check will be paid on the next regular pay day for the county. An employee who resigns without giving two weeks notice will not receive payment for accrued unused annual leave.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
632:
(a) Observed holidays. This section outlines the county's general practices related to eligibility and payment for holidays. The following holidays will be observed in all offices of the county:
New Year's Day | Martin Luther King, Jr. Day
Good Friday | Memorial Day
Independence Day | Labor Day
Veterans Day | Thanksgiving Day
Day after Thanksgiving | Christmas Eve Day
Christmas Day | Day after Christmas
(b) General policy. It shall be the policy of the county to ensure that all permanent full-time employees enjoy the same number of holidays each year. The standard shall be the number of holidays in a particular year which will be celebrated by permanent employees working a 40-hour week, Monday through Friday. For permanent employees on a workweek other than Monday through Friday, the Commission of Georgetown-Quitman County shall designate the workday that shall be observed. Permanent employees working less than full-time shall also be eligible to the above holidays with pay for their regular number of hours at their regular rate of pay.
(c) Holidays falling on weekends. Holidays falling on weekends will normally be observed as designated by the county manager. Employees whose duties require them to work on a holiday shall receive compensation for the holiday.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
633:
The county considers jury and witness duty an important community citizenship responsibility. Any employee shall be given necessary time off without loss of pay when performing jury duty or when required by proper authority to be a witness in legal proceedings. Employee will receive full pay for the necessary time off duty. County employees who perform jury duty or who are required to be a witness in a legal proceeding will be permitted to retain all fees and allowances received, therefore.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
634:
Lay-off is termination of employment of a career employee when, for any valid reason, it may be necessary to abolish one or more positions or reduce the number of employees in the county service. Lay-off does not reflect discredit on the service of the employee. The county commission shall be the final authority on lay-off decisions.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
635:
(a) When it is deemed in the best interest of the county service, a permanent status career employee or a department head may be granted leave of absence for personal or other reasons, provided the department head recommend such leave and approved by the county commission. The granted leave of absence period may not exceed one year. Valid reasons for leave of absence include, but are not confined to, prolonged illness or disability of the employee or members of the household; educational or training enrichment; pregnancy and childbirth; and military service.
(b) A leave of absence request must be submitted in writing in advance showing the employee's reason for requesting such leave of absence, plus a statement of intent to return to county service upon expiration of the leave of absence.
(c) Employees will be reinstated in their former positions when leave of absences are two months or less. The employee will waive reinstatement rights and privileges of the position after two months, although strong efforts will be made to return the employee to the former position or to a comparable position upon expiration of the period of leave of absence.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
636:
(a) Maternity leave will be treated as any other short-term disability leave without regard to paid/unpaid leave, benefit accruals, and county group insurance benefits.
(b) The employee shall determine commencement of maternity leave and is based solely on the employee's inability to work. It will be handled as a nonaccidental disability. An employee who takes maternity leave will be placed in a comparable position with the same salary as that at the time of taking leave. She will retain the original date of employment.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
637:

Reprimand is an oral or written notice of policy violation, mistakes, or other factors which may adversely influence employee's ability to efficiently carry out his duties and responsibilities. Any superior may reprimand a subordinate at any time for cause.

Bereavement pay used by Georgetown-Quitman County employees, three days with pay to attend business and funeral matters of immediate family. 650:
Suspension is the temporary removal of an employee from county service due to cause for a specified or indefinite period.
(1) Suspension for disciplinary reasons. An employee who does not continue to do his work at an acceptable level of competence as determined by his performance evaluations, who is insubordinate or uncooperative, who acts in a manner tending to lower discipline or morale within the county service, or who acts in a manner deemed not in the best interest of the county service or in its good repute may be suspended for a reasonable period of time, not to exceed 30 days, when alternative personnel actions (demotion, dismissal, fine, etc.) may not be warranted, appropriate or deemed in the best interest of the county service.
(2) Suspension pending a court decision. An employee may be suspended for a indefinite period when the county commission determines such action is necessary and in the best interest of the county service, in cases where an employee is charged with and awaiting trial for a criminal offense involving matters of prima facie prejudicial to the competent discharge of his duties and responsibilities. In these cases, the county commission may take such other action which they may deem necessary under the circumstances. After the employee has been tried and a verdict reached by the court or an entry of nolle prosequi has been made, the county commission shall make a final determination as to whether the employee shall be reinstated, dismissed or subject to whatever disciplinary action that may be considered to be necessary and appropriate in consideration of the facts of the case.
(3) Suspension during investigation of charges. When an employee has acted or is alleged to have acted in a manner which would subject him to dismissal from the county service, he may be suspended by the county commission for a period not in excess of one month while the county commission is investigating charges before making a final determination as to whether the employee would be dismissed from the county service. An employee who is exonerated of charges following investigation shall be reinstated without loss of pay, privileges, benefits, or status, retroactive to date of suspension.
(4) Suspension recommendations. When the department head deems such action is necessary, appropriate and in the best interest of the county service, a department head may recommend that an employee be suspended. The recommendation shall be in writing and shall contain the reasons why it is necessary for the department head to recommend suspension and the type and duration of the suspension. When alternative disciplinary personnel actions might be appropriate, the department head shall state why he selected suspension. The county commission may also initiate suspension.
(5) Delegation of suspension authority. The county commission may, at its discretion, delegate suspension authority to department heads, office heads, and selected division chiefs whenever it deems such delegation of authority is necessary to maintain the good order and good repute of the county services. Delegation of suspension authority shall be made in writing by the county commission.
(6) Notice of suspension. Upon notification of approval of a suspension recommendation, the county commission shall notify the employee in writing of the suspension and reasons therefore. A permanent status career employee shall be informed when he has the right to appeal a suspension. Probation status employees do not have the right of appeal.
(7) Suspension which may be appealed. Any suspension for disciplinary reasons or a suspension during an investigation of charges may be appealed pursuant to rule XII. A suspension pending a court decision may also be appealed, in which case consideration will be given only to whether the county commission's action was consistent with requirements of paragraph 8.04 of this rule and in the best interest of the county service. Appeals must be made within five work days of receipt of written notification of suspension, or suspension shall become final without further action.
(Ord. of 4-3-07)
651:

This article shall be known as the Quitman County Solid Waste Ordinance. It is the purpose of this article to provide for the healthy and sanitary management and disposal of solid waste in the county to ensure the public health, safety and welfare of the citizens of the county and encourage recycling of selected material through education and voluntary compliance. It shall apply to the preparation, storage, collection and disposal of all solid waste and shall prohibit unsanitary conditions in the unincorporated areas of the county, as presently or hereafter established.

672:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Ashes means the residue from the burning of wood, coal, coke or other combustible materials.
Bag means a flexible container with a hole at one end, capable of being closed by tying or twisting and made of plastic or other material designed and made to hold not over the number of pounds of household garbage set by the board of commissioners.
Brown goods means furniture, mattresses and similar residential or office furnishings.
Building material means any material defined as, but not limited to, lumber, brick, block, stone, carpet, plumbing materials, plaster, concrete, roofing, floor tile, gutters or other substances accumulated as a result of the construction of or repairs or additions to structures or accessory structures or the demolition of such.
Business trash means any accumulation of paper, cardboard, packaging materials, rags or accumulations other than garbage or household trash, which result from the operation of stores, offices and similar business or commercial enterprises.
Commercial establishment means any location open to the public or semipublic for the purpose of financial gain. Examples include, but are not limited to, retail stores, restaurants, hotels, storage units, hair salons, and banks. Mobile home parks and recreational vehicle (R.V.) rental park properties which are owned by a single entity are considered commercial establishments.
Commercial solid waste means all types of solid waste generated by stores, offices, restaurants, warehouses and other nonmanufacturing activities, excluding residential and industrial waste.
Container means a refuse receptacle and/or bags or sacks furnished by the county.
Disposal site means an area, location, tract of land or facility used or intended to be used for the disposal of solid waste, putrescible waste or other waste.
Garbage means the byproduct resulting from the growing, harvesting, processing, handling, preparation, cooking or consumption of animal or vegetable food, or other matter which is subject to decomposition, decay, putrefaction or the generation of noxious or offensive gases or odors, or which during or after decay may serve as breeding areas or feeding material for flies, insects or animals.
Hazardous refuse means solid wastes and other materials which:
(1) Have been defined as hazardous wastes pursuant to the Solid Waste Disposal Act (42 USC 6901 et seq.) or regulations promulgated by the state board of natural resources at chapter 391-3-11.
(2) Have been defined as hazardous substances pursuant to the Comprehensive Environmental Response Compensation and Liability Act (42 USC 9601 et seq.); or
(3) Constitute a hazard to health or safety, such as poison, acids, caustic matter or solutions, chemicals, infected materials, offal, fecal matter, explosives, radioactive materials and highly flammable substances.
Household trash means residential waste accumulation usually attendant upon housekeeping, such as paper, sweepings, dust, rags, bottles, cans or other residential refuse of any kind, other than garbage, excluding hazardous refuse, ashes and building material.
Industrial establishment means any establishment involved in the manufacture or assembly of a product or any part thereof.
Industrial waste means all waste, including solids, semisolids, sludge and liquids, created by or resulting from the operation of factories, processing plants or other manufacturing enterprises.
Laws means applicable federal, state and local laws, statutes, rules, regulations, ordinances and other governmental requirements.
Litter means all discarded manmade materials, including, but not limited to, garbage, household trash, industrial waste, building materials, appliances or portions thereof, refuse, waste materials, sand, gravel, slag, brickbats, rubbish, tin cans, trash, debris, dead animals or any other discarded, used or unconsumed substance which is not handled in accordance with the provisions of this article.
Loading and unloading area means a space or area used by any moving vehicle for the purpose of receiving, shipping and transporting goods, wares, commodities and persons.
Master-billed apartments, etc., means those residential apartment complexes where the solid waste billing is paid by the owner of the complex.
Mobile home park means a parcel of land which has been planned and improved for the placement of two or more mobile homes, or two or more recreational vehicles, for nontransient use and for rent.
Multiple family dwelling (multifamily) means a building designed for or occupied by two or more families, such as apartments, duplexes and triplexes.
Municipal solid waste means garbage and household trash, except hazardous refuse.
Person means any natural person, whether the owner, agent or tenant; any corporation, partnership, association, firm, receiver, guardian, trustee, executor, administrator, fiduciary, occupant, lessee, tenant or representative of any of the same.
Public property and private property mean the right-of-way of any road or highway; any body of water or watercourse or the shores or beaches thereof; any park, playground, building, refuge or conservation or recreation area; and residential or farm properties, timberlands or forests.
Refuse means solid waste accumulations consisting of any combination of ashes, building material, garbage, hazardous refuse, household trash and other waste or discarded materials of all kinds.
Refuse receptacle means a container or bag approved by the county as acceptable for the temporary reception and storage of refuse pending transportation to a permanent disposal site. The term shall include plastic bags where approved by the county.
Rules and regulations means the detailed rules and regulations approved by the board of commissioners the board or its designee is authorized to use and enforce for the efficient and safe operation of this article.
Sanitation fee means the amount to be paid by the persons and entities responsible under the terms of this article for the sanitary handling or disposal of solid waste by the county or their designee.
Scavenge and scavenging mean the unauthorized and uncontrolled retrieval of discarded refuse materials.
White goods means appliances such as stoves and refrigerators.
Yard trimmings means leaves, brush, grass clippings, shrub and tree prunings, discarded Christmas trees, nursery and greenhouse vegetative residuals, and vegetative matter resulting from landscaping development and maintenance other than mining, agricultural and silvicultural operations.

674:
The following practices and procedures shall be followed by persons in the unincorporated areas of the county in order to facilitate the collection of solid waste:
(1) Refuse. All refuse shall be managed by such persons in accordance with applicable laws and all municipal solid waste shall be placed and maintained in containers satisfying the requirements of this article and of the rules and regulations of the county. Containers shall be maintained at all times with tightfitting lids or covers, and secured in such manner as to prevent the overturning by the elements or by dogs or other animals.
(2) Garbage. Garbage placed in containers for collection shall be enclosed in paper or plastic bags. Garbage shall be drained of all liquids prior to its being placed in refuse receptacles or bags.
(3) Injurious trash items. Municipal solid waste or refuse brought to the county transfer station with a potential for inflicting injury, such as broken glass, lightbulbs, sharp pieces of metal, fluorescent tubes and television tubes shall be securely packaged or wrapped in such a manner as will prevent injury to the collection crews or other persons and to prevent the puncture of the bags. The provisions of this subsection shall not apply to material placed in mechanically handled containers.
(4) Hazardous refuse. Hazardous refuse will not be collected by the county. No person shall place any hazardous refuse in any refuse receptacle or other container for collection by the county and shall not haul or deliver any hazardous refuse to the county transfer station. All applicable laws relating to the generation, management, handling, treatment, storage or disposal of hazardous refuse shall be observed by all persons, and the county reserves the right to report any discovered or known violations of such laws to the appropriate state, federal or local authorities.
(5) Building materials. Building materials will not be collected by the county. The owner of the premises or the contractor, builder or person doing the repairs, remodeling, construction or demolition shall be required to haul and transfer the debris to the county transfer station.
(6) Tree and vegetable removal by home occupants. Trees cut by the owner or occupant shall be taken to the county transfer station by the owner. When a tree is cut from private property by anyone other than the owner, such person shall remove and legally dispose of all wood and limbs. The owner, tenant or other persons in possession of the property shall be responsible to see that such tree trimmer or other person outlined above complies with this provision.
(7) Other. Grass clippings, leaves, pine straw and/or pine cones shall be disposed of as provided in subsection (6) of this section.
(8) Ashes. It shall be unlawful to deposit hot ashes in garbage containers or bags. Cooled ashes may be deposited in bags. Loose ashes or clinkers shall not be placed or deposited upon streets, sidewalks or side parks.
(9) Pet litter. Pet litter must be placed in securely tied bags, not to exceed ten pounds in weight, and placed in the container, when containers are used by the county.
(10) Household furniture and furnishings. Household furniture, furnishings and brown goods shall be disposed of as provided in subsection (6) of this section.
(11) Appliances. Appliances (white goods) shall be disposed of as provided in subsection (6) of this section.
(12) Disposable diapers. Disposable diapers must be placed and tied securely in bags and placed in the regular container or bags.
(Ord. of 10-12-1998, § III)
675:
(a) Residential. (a) No person shall construct a municipal solid waste handling facility in the county until such person has at his expense prepared and the board has approved a health and environmental baseline assessment study. Within the designated area the study shall assess the current levels in humans, animals, plants, soil and water of contaminants which could be released from the proposed facility and the current status of human and animal health and environmental quality using measures appropriate to the contaminants which could be released from the proposed facility. The study shall establish a database and baseline indices which will provide sufficient data for measuring and determining what, if any, health, safety or environmental impacts may occur as a result of releases from the facility.
(b) The board or its designated health representative shall participate to the full extent desired by the board in the study design and execution. The study design, methodology and form shall require advance approval of the board or its designated health representative.
(c) The database shall include:
(1) A collection of relevant human cell samples including plasma, urine, hair, nail samples and other appropriate samples from humans living within the designated area; representative samples of all wildlife in the designated area; representative samples of animals and animal products from the designated area which are eaten by humans; representative samples of vegetables and produce grown in the designated area; soil samples taken on-site and in the designated area; and water samples from surface water and groundwater in the designated area. The collection of samples shall be conducted under the supervision of the board or a designated board representative.
(2) The determination of the baseline rate for all known or suspected health effects which may be caused by exposure to contaminants which could be released from the facility.
(3) A profile of the demographic characteristics, including, but not limited to, age, sex and race of individuals, supplying samples and residing in the designated area.
(d) The sample size for the collection of human data shall be that number of individuals which will produce an 80 percent power to detect as significant, P≤0.05, a twofold increase in the rate, of the adverse health outcome of interest. The individuals who constitute the sample population shall be identified by moving out in concentric circles from the release point until the required sample size is achieved.

No person, firm or corporation shall treat, or cause, suffer or allow to be treated, any biomedical waste within the unincorporated areas of the county except by one of the following methods; provided, however, that such method of treatment is first approved by the director of the environmental protection division of the state department of natural resources:
(1) Incineration in the thermal treatment technology facility which provides complete combustion of waste to render it nonpathogenic.
a. Biomedical waste thermal treatment technology facilities shall be capable of maintaining a minimum temperature in the primary chamber sufficient to destroy infectious agents and produce a residue essentially free of odors and unstable organic matter. If chemotherapy wastes are incinerated, the facility must be capable of maintaining a minimum of 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit in the secondary combustion chamber and a minimum residence time of two seconds.
b. Atmospheric emissions shall be controlled so as not to exceed air quality standards of the division.
(2) Decontamination by heating with steam under pressure (autoclave) so as to render the biomedical waste noninfectious.
a. A recording thermometer shall be used during each complete cycle to ensure the attainment of a temperature of 121 degrees Celsius (250 degrees Fahrenheit) for one-half hour or longer in order to achieve decontamination of the entire load.
b. Monitoring of the steam sterilization process shall be required in order to confirm the attainment of decontamination.
c. Monitoring may be through the use of biological indicators or other methods as approved by the director. Indicators used to ensure the attainment of the proper temperature during steam sterilization shall be placed at the point of the load where the rate of thermal penetration is at a minimum.
(3) Other methods as may be approved by the director.
(Ord. of 6-14-1994(1), § 3)

An ordinance of Quitman County, Georgia, establishing rules and regulations governing the subdivision of land into streets, blocks and lots, requiring street improvements and the installation of utilities as a condition of plat approval, defining terms, establishing procedures, providing penalties for violation, repealing ordinances and for other purposes.

Interpretation of Certain Terms or Words.
Except as specifically defined herein, all words used in this resolution have their customary dictionary definitions for the purpose of this resolution, certain words or terms used herein are defined as follows:
Words used in the present tense include the future tense. Words used in the singular include the plural, and words used in the plural include the singular.
The word "shall" is always mandatory and not merely directory.
The word "may" is permissive.
The word "lot" includes the word "plot" or "parcel."
The word "structure" includes the word "building."
The word "person" includes a firm, association, organization, partnership, trust, company, or corporation, as well as an individual.
The word "used" or "occupied," as applied to any land or building, shall be construed to include the words "intended," "arranged," or "designed to be used or occupied."
The word "map" shall mean the Official Map of Quitman County, Georgia, and may include a series of maps in sections.
The term "Building Inspector" refers to the person subsequently and specifically designated by the County Commissioners and so employed as the Building Inspector for Quitman County, or authorized representative of that office.
The term "Board of Appeals" refers to the Board of Appeals of Quitman County, Georgia.
The term "County Clerk" refers to the County Administrator of Quitman County, Georgia, or authorized representative of that office.
The term "County Inspector" refers to the person subsequently and specifically designated by the County Commissioners and so employed as the person to serve as the County Inspector to insure all ordinances of the County are complied with, and as such has the authority of the Board of Commissioners.
The terms "Commission" or "County Commission" refer to the legally constituted and elected governing body of Quitman County, Georgia.
3.01 Accessory. A use or building subordinate to the principal building on a lot used for purposes customarily identical to the main or principal use or building located on the same lot herewith.
3.02 Alley. A secondary way which affords vehicular service access to the side or rear of abutting property.
3.03 Alteration of Building. Any change in the supporting members of a building (such as bearing walls, columns, or girders); an addition or reduction to a building; any change in use; or relocation of a building from one location or position to another.
3.04 Boarding, Lodging, or Rooming House. A dwelling in which meals or lodging or both are provided.
3.05 Building. A structure which is completely enclosed by a roof and by exterior walls which is [are] moveable or permanently affixed to [a] lot and used or intended for the shelter, support, or enclosure of persons, animals, or property of any kind.
3.06 Building, Principal. A building in which is conducted the principal use of the lot on which said building is situated.
3.07 Building Line. That line which represents the distance a building or structure must be set back from a lot boundary or a street right-of-way line according to the terms of this resolution. In all cases the building lines of a lot shall be determined to run parallel to and set back an appropriate distance required within the district in which the lot is located from street right-of-way lines, street centerlines, or other lot boundary lines.
3.08 Canopy, Free Standing. No limitation to visibility; front[,] side and corner yard offsets to be [a] minimum of 15 feet.
3.09 Conditional Use. A use (sometimes called a "special exception," but not to be confused with a "variance") that would not be appropriate generally or without restriction but which, if controlled as to number, area, location, or relation to the neighborhood, would not be injurious to the public health, safety, welfare, morals, order, comfort, convenience, appearance, or general welfare.
3.10 Clinic. An establishment where medical or dental patients who are not lodged overnight are admitted for examination or treatment.
3.11 Cluster Development. A change from the conventional pattern of subdivision development which groups housing units into relatively tight units while providing a unified network of open space. A variety of housing types may be utilized in clusters, including single-family, town houses, apartments, and condominiums.
3.12 District. The term applied to various geographical areas for purposes of interpreting the provisions of this ordinance. The terms "district" and "zoning district" are synonymous and are used interchangeably throughout this resolution.
3.13 Dwelling. A building or portion of a building arranged or designed to provide living quarters for one or more families. The terms "dwelling," "dwelling units," and "residence," are synonymous. (See definition of "family," 3.20).
3.14 Dwelling, One-Family. A detached dwelling designed for or occupied exclusively by one (1) family on a single lot.
3.15 Dwelling, Two-Family. A dwelling arranged or designed to be occupied by two (2) families in separate dwelling units living independently of each other on a single lot.
3.16 Dwelling, Group. A building or portion of a building occupied or intended for occupancy by a number of unrelated persons or families, but in which separate cooking facilities are not provided for such resident persons or families. The term "group dwelling" includes, but is not limited to, the terms rooming house, apartment, hotel, retirement home, nursing home, fraternity or sorority home, Y.M.C.A., Y.W.C.A. and similar organizational or institutional group. A transient hotel, motel, or tourist home shall not be deemed to be [a] group dwelling as herein defined.
3.17 Dwelling, Multiple-Family. A building or series of buildings on the same lot or portions thereof used or designed and rented as dwellings for three (3) or more families living independently of each other, with the number of families in residence not exceeding the number of dwelling units provided. The terms "multiple-family" and "multifamily" are synonymous.
3.18 Dwelling Unit. One or more rooms connected together and constituting a separate, independent housekeeping establishment (for use on a basis involving owner occupancy or rental lease) on a weekly, monthly, or longer basis, with provisions for cooking, eating, and sleeping, and physically set apart from any other dwelling units in the same structure.
3.19 Drive-In. A retail or service enterprise oriented to automobile-driving patrons wherein service is provided to the consumer on the outside and/or inside of the principal building. The term "drive-in" includes drive-in restaurants, dairy bars, theaters, banks, and car washes.
3.20 Family. One or more persons with the generic character of a family unit occupying a single dwelling unit and using common cooking facilities, provided that servants and agricultural employees employed on the premises may be housed on the premises.
3.21 Garage, Public. Any garage, other than a private garage, which is used for [the] storage, repair, rental, servicing, washing, adjusting, or equipping of automobiles or other vehicles.
3.22 Garage, Private. An accessory building or portion of a principal building used only for the private storage of motor vehicles as an accessory use.
3.23 Garage, Repair. Buildings and premises designed or used for repairing motor vehicles, trailers, and related transport carriers, provided that body work and painting shall be conducted within fully enclosed buildings and provided further that trailers and self-propelled vehicles in process of repair shall be stored in a fully enclosed and screened area.
3.24 Home Occupation. Any use conducted entirely within a dwelling and carried on by the occupants thereof, which use is clearly incidental and secondary to the use of the dwelling for residential purposes.
3.25 Junk or Salvage Yards. The use of any part of a lot, whether inside or outside of a building, for the storage, keeping, abandonment, sale or resale of junk, salvage, or scrap materials, or the dismantling, demolition, or abandonment of buildings, automobiles, or other vehicles, machinery, equipment or parts thereof.
3.26 Loading Space. Off-street. Space logically and conveniently located for pickups and deliveries off public rights-of-way, scaled to delivery vehicles expected to be used and acceptable to such vehicles at all times.
3.27 Lot. An area designed as a separate and distinct parcel of land or a legally recorded subdivision plot of land in a legally recorded deed as filed in the official county records.
3.28 Lot, Corner. A lot located at the intersection of two or more streets.
3.29 Lot, Double-Frontage. A lot which has frontage on more than one street, provided, however, that no corner lot shall qualify as a double-frontage lot unless said corner lot has frontage on three or more streets.
3.30 Lot Width. The distance between side lot lines measured at the front building line.
3.31 Manufactured Home. "Manufactured home" means a new or used structure, transportable in one or more sections, which, in the traveling mode, is eight body feet or more in width or 40 body feet or more in length or, when erected on site, is 320 or more square feet and which is built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used as a dwelling with or without a permanent foundation when connected to the required utilities and includes the plumbing, heating, air-conditioning, and electrical systems contained therein; except that such term shall include any structure which meets all the requirements of this paragraph except the size requirements and with respect to which the manufacturer voluntarily files a certification required by the secretary of housing and urban development and complies with the standards established under the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974, 42 USC Section 5401, et seq. The term "manufactured home" is not synonymous with the term "mobile home," "doublewide" or "home trailer" (see paragraph 3.301), nor does it include "recreational vehicles" (see 3.38); but includes "modular home" and "prefabricated homes." Every manufactured home shall:
(a) be suitable for year-round occupancy;
(b) be placed on a permanent masonry foundation so as to be substantially fixed as to its site;
(c) be connected to an approved water supply, approved waste disposal system, and electrical supply similar to site-built housing; and
(d) be landscaped with trees, shrubs, and other plant material substantially equal to or better than one-family dwellings within five-hundred (500) feet.
3.311 Mobile Home. "Mobile home" means a new or used structure, transportable in one or more sections, which in the traveling mode, is eight body feet or more in width or 40 body feet or more in length, or, when erected on site, is 320 or more square feet and which is built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used as a dwelling with or without a permanent foundation when connected to the required utilities and includes the plumbing, heating, air-conditioning, and electrical systems contained therein and built prior to June 15, 1976. The term does not include "recreational vehicles" (see 3.38). Every mobile home shall:
(a) be suitable for year-round occupancy;
(b) be placed on a permanent masonry foundation so as to be substantially fixed to its site;
(c) be connected to an approved water supply, approved waste disposal system, and electrical supply similar to site-built housing;
(d) be landscaped with trees, shrubs, and other plant material substantially equal to or better than one-family dwellings within five-hundred (500) feet;
3.32 Mobile Home Park. A parcel of land which has been planned and improved for the placement of two (2) or more mobile homes for non-transient use. A permit shall be required for the establishment of a mobile home park. The term "park" includes the term "community."
3.33 Motel. A building or buildings in which lodging is provided and offered to the public for compensation, which is open to transient or permanent guests. The word "motel" includes the terms "motor hotel" and "tourist court."
3.34 Nonconforming Use. A structure or land lawfully occupied by an existing use which does not conform with the permitted uses for the zoning districts in which it is situated, either [on] May 9, 1995, or as the result of subsequent amendments to this resolution.
3.35 Parking Lot. Any public or private open area used for the express purpose of parking automobiles and other vehicles, with the exception of areas on the premises of single-family dwellings used for parking purposes incidental to the principal use. Parking lots may be the principal use on a given lot or an accessory use.
3.36 Parking Space. A space not less than nine (9) by eighteen (18) feet plus maneuvering space within a parking lot or on a single-family dwelling lot expressly provided for [the] purpose of parking an automobile or other vehicle.
2.37 [3.37] Patio House. A single-family dwelling in which most or all of a lot is used with yard space combined instead of divided. Front, rear, and side yards are consolidated into one garden area, either partially or completely bordered by rooms or enclosed by walls.
3.38 Planned Unit Development (PUD). A group of three (3) or more buildings constructed on a plot of un-subdivided ground at least two (2) acres in size, which provides for common open spaces and a variety of choice in housing types and land utilization. Land ownership or rental patterns may vary, with rental units, cooperatives, and condominiums being choices open to PUD developers. If common open spaces, including streets, are not dedicated for public use, legal agreements shall be provided for approval by the County Commission and shall include [a] provision for adequate future maintenance. The terms "planned unit development" and "PUD" are interchangeable.
3.39 Recreational Vehicle. A vehicular, portable structure built on a chassis, designed to be either pulled by another vehicle or self-propelled, to be used as a temporary dwelling for travel and recreational purposes. The term "recreational vehicle" includes the terms "RV," "motor home," "travel trailer," and related wheeled recreational equipment not designed for year-round occupancy.
3.40 Roadside Stand. A small-scale business structure permanently or seasonally located within an agricultural or rural area for the sale of agricultural products primarily produced on the premises and using only signs that are removed during seasons when the business is closed.
3.41 Sign. The term "sign" shall mean and include every outdoor advertising device, billboard, poster, panel, freestanding ground sign, roof sign, projecting sign, pylon sign, illuminated sign, sign painted on a wall, window, marquee, awning or canopy, and shall include any announcement, declaration, demonstration, display, ribbon, banner, illustration, or insignia used to advertise or promote the interests of any person when the same is placed in view of the general public traveling along a public street or road right-of-way.
3.42 Signs, Number and Surface Area. For the purpose of determining number of signs, a sign shall be considered to be a single display surface or display device containing elements organized, related, and composed to form a unit. Where matter is displayed in a random manner without organized relationship of elements, or where there is reasonable doubt about the relationship of elements, each element shall be considered to be a single sign. The surface area of a sign shall be computed as including the entire area within a regular geometric form or combinations of regular geometric forms comprising all of the display area of the sign and including all of the elements of the matter displayed. Frames and structural members not bearing advertising matter shall not be included in computation of surface area.
3.43 Sign, On-Site. An outdoor advertising device relating in its subject matter to the premises on which it is located, or to products, accommodations, services, or activities on the premises. The terms "point-of-sale" sign and "on-premises" signs are synonymous with "on-site" sign.
3.44 Sign, Off-Site. An outdoor advertising device other than an on-site including those erected by the outdoor advertising industry.
3.45 Street. A dedicated and accepted public right-of-way for vehicular traffic which affords the principal means of access to abutting properties.
3.46 Structure. Anything constructed or erected, the use of which requires a fixed location on the ground or which is attached to something having a fixed location on the ground.
3.47 Tourist Home. A dwelling in which sleeping accommodations in less than ten (10) rooms are provided or offered for the use of guests in return for compensation. Any dwelling in which such accommodations are offered in ten (10) or more rooms shall be deemed to be a hotel as herein defined. The use of a dwelling as a tourist home shall not be considered as an accessory use nor a customary home occupation.
3.48 Tract. See "Lot," 3.27.
3.49 Use, Accessory. See "Accessory," 3.01.
3.50 Use, Conditional. See "Conditional Use," 3.08.
3.51 Use, Principal. The primary purpose for which a lot is occupied and/or used.
3.52 Variance. A modification of the strict terms of this resolution granted by the Board of Appeals where such modification will not be contrary to the public good, such as irregular lot size, topographic or other characteristics of the land, and not as the result of any action on the part of the property owner, a literal enforcement of this resolution would result in unnecessary and undue hardship.
3.53 Wetlands. Those lands classified as "poorly or very poorly drained soils" by the U.S. Department of Agriculture Soil Conservation Service in the Soil Survey of Quitman County, Georgia.
3.54 Yard. A required space on the same lot with a principal building, open, unoccupied, and unobstructed by buildings or structures from ground to sky except where encroachments of accessory buildings and other structures are expressly permitted.
3.55 Yard, Front. A yard situated between the front building line and the front lot line and extending the full width of the lot.
3.56 Yard, Rear. A yard situated between the rear building line and the rear lot line and extending the full width of the lot.
3.57 Yard, Side. A yard situated between a side building line and the front yard to the rear yard.
869: From and after May 9, 1995, the Quitman County Commission shall be the platting authority.
870: No construction work shall be undertaken on a proposed land subdivision until a preliminary plat has been approved by the Board of Commissioners and the requirements of Section 706 have been satisfied.
871: No plat of a land subdivision shall be accepted for recording in the office of the Clerk of the Superior Court of Quitman County except a final plat on which is inscribed the approval of the County Commission.

873:
No building shall be erected on any lot unless the street giving access thereto has been accepted as a public street or approved by the Commission as a private street as having been constructed in conformity with the County standards in accordance with this ordinance, or unless such street has attained the legal status of a public street prior to May 9, 1995, or has been accepted as a public street by the County Commission.
